text:
Henry's total bike trip is 60 miles. He first stopped after traveling 20 miles from the start. His second stop was 15 miles before the end, meaning he had traveled 60 - 15 = 45 miles from the start when he made his second stop. The distance between the first stop (20 miles) and the second stop (45 miles) is 45 - 20 = 25 miles.

Answer: 25
reasoning:
We are given: "Henry made two stops during his 60-mile bike trip. He first stopped after 20 miles. His second stop was 15 miles before the end of the trip. How many miles did he travel between his first and second stops?"

Total trip = 60 miles.
First stop: after 20 miles from start.
Second stop: 15 miles before the end of the trip (so distance from start to second stop = 60 - 15 = 45 miles).

Distance between first and second stops = distance from start to second stop - distance from start to first stop = 45 - 20 = 25 miles.

Answer: 25.
